reference_fields: JAPS History Origin and Classification of Persimmon Cultivars
Robert Nissen and Robin E. Roberts
Journal of the American Pomological Society 69(1):31-44 review of persimmon origin, production, classification, and major cultivars

categories.name: Commercial persimmon cultivars discussed by region
categories.description: Nissen and Roberts discuss these persimmon cultivars in regional production and commercialization context

categories.name: PCNA Japanese persimmon cultivars with genetic origins
categories.description: Nissen and Roberts list these PCNA Japanese persimmon cultivars with bud sport, mutation, or parentage notes in Table 4

fields.category: Commercial persimmon cultivars discussed by region

rows.name: Fuyu
rows.description: Nissen and Roberts say Fuyu is the dominant global non-astringent persimmon cultivar, important in Japan, Korea, Brazil, Australia, and New Zealand

rows.name: Jiro
rows.description: Nissen and Roberts discuss Jiro as a non-astringent cultivar that loses astringency early in warm climates and is one of the two main Australian cultivars

rows.name: Luo Tian Tian Shi
rows.description: Nissen and Roberts describe Luo Tian Tian Shi as an exceptional Chinese PCNA cultivar with a dominant trait for astringency loss on the tree

rows.name: Hiratanenashi
rows.description: Nissen and Roberts say Hiratanenashi is one of the astringent cultivars representing a substantial share of Japanese production

rows.name: Tone Wase
rows.description: Nissen and Roberts say Tone Wase is one of the astringent cultivars representing a substantial share of Japanese production and list it as a bud sport of Hiratanenashi

rows.name: Taubate
rows.description: Nissen and Roberts list Taubate as an astringent persimmon cultivar grown in Brazil

rows.name: Rama Forte
rows.description: Nissen and Roberts list Rama Forte as a PVA astringent persimmon cultivar grown in Brazil

rows.name: Chocolate
rows.description: Nissen and Roberts list Chocolate as a local persimmon cultivar grown in Brazil

rows.name: Manteiga
rows.description: Nissen and Roberts list Manteiga as a local persimmon cultivar grown in Brazil

rows.name: Kaki Tipo
rows.description: Nissen and Roberts say Mediterranean persimmon production is based partly on Kaki Tipo and that Italy historically based most production on it

rows.name: Rojo Brillante
rows.description: Nissen and Roberts say Rojo Brillante is increasing in popularity in Spain and the Mediterranean because of quality and productivity

rows.name: Triumph
rows.description: Nissen and Roberts say Triumph is important in Mediterranean production and forms most of the Israeli crop

rows.name: Coroa de Rei
rows.description: Nissen and Roberts describe Coroa de Rei as the most important cultivar grown in Portugal

rows.name: Hana Fuyu
rows.description: Nissen and Roberts list Hana Fuyu among cultivars grown in Portugal

rows.name: O'Gosho
rows.description: Nissen and Roberts list O'Gosho among cultivars grown in Portugal

rows.name: Gordo
rows.description: Nissen and Roberts say Gordo is the main cultivar in the Cataluna region of Spain, though under threat from Rojo Brillante

rows.name: Thach That
rows.description: Nissen and Roberts list Thach That as a major cultivar in northern Vietnam

rows.name: Nhan Hau
rows.description: Nissen and Roberts list Nhan Hau as a major cultivar in northern Vietnam

rows.name: Luc Yen
rows.description: Nissen and Roberts list Luc Yen as a major cultivar in northern Vietnam

rows.name: Trung Loc
rows.description: Nissen and Roberts list Trung Loc as a cultivar used in central and southern Vietnam

rows.name: Vuong
rows.description: Nissen and Roberts list Vuong as a cultivar used in central and southern Vietnam

fields.category: PCNA Japanese persimmon cultivars with genetic origins

rows.name: Imoto
rows.description: Nissen and Roberts list Imoto as possibly a bud sport of Jiro

rows.name: Uenishiwase
rows.description: Nissen and Roberts list Uenishiwase as a bud sport of Matsumotowase Fuyu

rows.name: Sunami
rows.description: Nissen and Roberts list Sunami as a bud sport of Fuyu

rows.name: Aisyuhou
rows.description: Nissen and Roberts list Aisyuhou as a bud sport of Manekawa-Jiro

rows.name: Tanbawase-Fuyu
rows.description: Nissen and Roberts list Tanbawase-Fuyu as a bud sport of Fuyu

rows.name: Kyi-joh
rows.description: Nissen and Roberts list Kyi-joh as a bud sport of Matsunotowase Fuyu

rows.name: Ohtanenashi
rows.description: Nissen and Roberts list Ohtanenashi as a bud sport of Hiratanenashi

rows.name: Kohshimaru
rows.description: Nissen and Roberts list Kohshimaru as a bud sport of Hiratanenashi

rows.name: Suruga
rows.description: Nissen and Roberts list Suruga as a cross of Hana Gosho and Oku Gosho

rows.name: Izu
rows.description: Nissen and Roberts list Izu as a cross of Fuyu and Okitu-1, where Okitu-1 is from Okugosho x Okugosho

rows.name: Shinshu
rows.description: Nissen and Roberts list Shinshu as a cross involving Okitsu-20 and Okitsu-1

rows.name: Youhou
rows.description: Nissen and Roberts list Youhou as a cross of Fuyu and Jiro

rows.name: Taishu
rows.description: Nissen and Roberts list Taishu as a cross of Fuyu and IIiG-16, with IIiG-16 from Jiro and an Okugosho x Hanagosho parent

rows.name: Kanshu
rows.description: Nissen and Roberts list Kanshu as a cross involving Shinshu 318-4, Fuyu, and an Okugosho x Hanagosho parent

rows.name: Kishu
rows.description: Nissen and Roberts list Kishu as a cross involving Izu, Akitsu-5, Fuyu, and an Okugosho x Hanagosho parent
